title: Wiltshire Hunt Sabs uncover horrific scenes at industrial-scale gamebird rearing site
content:
Dead gamebirds burned in bonfire pits in breach of animal by-product regulations

Guest post by Wiltshire Hunt Sabs: In July, after being alerted alerted to illegal practises at a local shoot, they paid a visit to the Stockton Shoot in Wiltshire and what they found was truly horrific – a bonfire full of dead charred birds, set next to the industrial sized operation.

Bordering the shoot is Stockton Wood and Down a 61.5 hectare Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI), situated within approximately 500metres of the rearing pens. The site supports a diverse range of flora, including several rare and notable plant species, while its birdlife includes buzzards, green and great spotted woodpeckers, nuthatches, nightingales, lesser whitethroats and grasshopper warblers.

The environmental impacts of intensive pheasant releases are well documented. High densities of released gamebirds can alter woodland ecosystems, damage sensitive ground flora, enrich soils with excessive nutrients and cause long-term degradation around release pens. Guidance recommends rotating pen locations to allow habitats to recover and to provide fresh ground for successive flocks.

author: hsa_oryx
title: SHOOTING’S REVOLVING DOOR: BLOODSPORTS IN THE HALLS OF POWER
content:
With the current parliamentary reshuffles going on, the HSA shooting team takes a look at the influence of shooting interests in parliament in recent times.

As has been widely covered in various HSA exposes , as well as by Animal Aid and more recently End Bird Shooting the pheasant and partridge shooting industry would struggle to survive at scale without industrial game bird farming. Many exposes have shown that birds trapped on game farms suffer similar uses and abuses to any other animal found on a factory farm. Who would have thought that a past time of wealthy landowners would receive a pretty large helping hand in getting their sick thrills.

Code of Practice sets the Paice for game birds

DEFRA has a Code of Practice which outlines so-called best practice throughout the industry, though its conditions are barely legally binding. The contents of this Code of Practice were largely shaped by Tory MP James Paice, who was also a director of the Game & Wildlife Conservation Trust (GWCT), as well as a member of the British Association for Shooting & Conservation (BASC). One of his first tasks as a DEFRA minister was to withdraw a Code of Practice which would have prevented keeping pheasants in cages for their entire egg laying lives. title: “Cruel And Illegal” Hare Hunt Celebrated At Hunting Festival
content:
The Stowe School Beagles – dubbed “cruel and illegal” by Northamptonshire Police – have won a major prize at hunting’s showcase event, the Festival of Hounds.

Last week the HSA reported on the event, a dismal gathering of hardcore hunters on a patch of waste ground near the A1.

Not only were the Stowe, who were convicted of brutally killing a hare just weeks ago, allowed to participate in the event, they won the best Doghound category in the beagle show!

This year the so-called festival was run by the British Hound Sports Association, an outfit that claims to be the regulatory body of hunting. However, instead of investigating the Stowe Beagles, the BHSA has lauded them in the showring: as we have said from the outset, the Festival of Hounds is a celebration of illegal hunting.

Early signs had been that the Stowe Beagles were attempting to keep a low profile. Stowe’s Headteacher – a puppy walker for the hunt – has ignored our polite letter expressing concern at the activities of the pack and removed the reference to hunt kennelman Philip Kennedy from their website.

However, their appearance at the Festival of Hounds is a grim but predictable reminder that hunters will stop at nothing to persecute our wildlife.

title: PETERING OUT IN PETERBOROUGH: THE 2026 FESTIVAL OF HOUNDS
content:
Today the ever-shrinking hunting world will gather at the east of England Showground near Peterborough for their annual Festival of Hounds. For decades, this event was known as the Festival of Hunting but – as so often in the hunting world – language has been changed to hide their real intent.

Fittingly, the Festival is now run by the inept British Hound Sports Association, itself a lame rebrand of the Hunting Office – the organisation that promotes trail hunting as a “smokescreen” to conceal illegal hunting. Predictably, one of the foxhound judges this year is Hunting Office Webinar star Richard Tyacke, while BHSA luminary and convicted foxhunting criminal Julian Barnfield will deliver a demonstration of hound judging.

Considering the ongoing Coniston Foxhounds case and the recent conviction of the Stowe School Beagles – where youngsters were visibly involved in killing hunted animals – it is troubling to note that the event includes a Young Handlers Class which “was introduced to celebrate the many young people that help in kennels. ” Over twenty years after the passing of the Hunting Act why are youngsters still being inducted into the world of hunting?

author: webadmin
title: HOWL – Hounds Off Our Wildlife
content:
HOWL – the magazine of the Hunt Saboteurs Association – has just hit the doormats of our thousands of members. As usual, it is packed with news from the front line in the fight against all blood sports.

This forty-page edition is packed with articles on a huge range of topics including: the scourge of violence against women sabs; the growing problem of catapult-related animal abuse; and an update on our parliamentary campaign. As usual, this edition also features our regular Group News from our network of 60-plus affiliated groups across the country.

All HOWL articles are written by hunt sabs and others exclusively for the magazine: you won’t find HOWL content anywhere else. And – in keeping with our grassroots, direct action ethos – the magazine is commissioned, edited and distributed by a volunteer team, meaning more of your subscription is ploughed back into the campaign.

HOWL is published three times a year and has been in continuous production since 1973, making it by far the oldest – and best! – animal rights magazine in the world. So, if you would like to start receiving HOWL, please join the Hunt Saboteurs Association here .
